result.headline: Control fault: output ch[3] saturated at 1900 from t=52.1 s; pitch tracking failed, also early at t=0.9-5.7 s.
result.explanation: Two control faults. One: early pitch divergence at t=0.9-5.7 s with a battery and sensor-health warning. Two: ch[3] stuck at 1900 us from t=52.142 s, followed by inverted pitch response and yaw spin. Component not identified.

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[3]] at t=52.142 s: 1497 -> 1900 us (step 403, 201.5x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: ch[3] jumps to its limit first in the late sequence; cc_11 shows it stays at 1900 for the rest of the recording (min=max=1900).

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[pitch] followed its setpoint worse from t=55.301 to 69.126 s: typical |error| up to 23.71 deg against 6.053 over the whole recording
evidence.shows: Pitch control degrades after ch[3] saturates. Over 55-69 s the pitch response is inverted (corr -0.909 at 1.681 s lag), while roll still tracks (corr 0.965 at 0.721 s lag).

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[pitch] diverged from its setpoint from t=0.897 to 5.666 s (peak |error| 42.409 deg)
evidence.shows: Early divergence. Setpoint went to about -20 deg while pitch rose to about +20 deg. ch[2] followed the setpoint (1140 us), so the command was sensible but the aircraft did not respond that way.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=1.015 s controller.event[mavros: Battery] mavros: Battery: WARN: Low voltage
evidence.shows: Low-voltage warning at t=1.015 s, together with the sensor-health error at line 23. Same time as the early pitch divergence; throttle fell from 47 to 3 %.

evidence.quote: CHANGE vehicle.attitude[yaw] at t=29.572 s: -19.113 -> -63.628 deg (step -44.516, 99.9x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: Large yaw steps at t=29.6, 42.4 and 65.0 s, and the yaw reaches -279.9 deg. This points to large uncontrolled yaw motion and/or an unreliable attitude estimate.

checked.check: Order in which signals left baseline in 52-70 s
checked.result: ch[3] left baseline first (t=52.142, 1900 us), then ch[4] and ch[5], yaw, ch[1], and the roll setpoint at 53.492. Pitch left baseline last (t=65.785).
checked.about: Actuator output channel ch[3] as the earliest sign of the late fault

checked.check: Pitch setpoint vs pitch in 55-69 s
checked.result: Correlation -0.253 at zero lag, -0.909 at 1.681 s lag. Typical difference 20.782 deg, worst 40.333 deg.
checked.about: Pitch control inverted or lost. Mechanism unclear: could be stuck surface, estimator or sensor fault, or loss of control.

checked.check: Roll setpoint vs roll in 55-69 s
checked.result: Correlation 0.965 at 0.721 s lag. Typical difference 9.626 deg, with a worst case of 59.16 deg at 62.871 s.
checked.about: Whole-controller or communication failure (roll still tracks)

checked.result: Pitch went to about +20 deg against a setpoint of about -20 deg. Throttle fell from 47 to 3 % then rose to 54 %. Altitude fell from 71.078 to 45.936 m. No signal left baseline before the events.
checked.about: Power / sensor-health versus controller cause of the early divergence

effects.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[pitch] followed its setpoint worse from t=55.301 to 69.126 s: typical |error| up to 23.71 deg against 6.053 over the whole recording
effects.why: Pitch degradation starts after the ch[3] saturation at t=52.142 s, and pitch was the last signal to leave baseline.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.attitude[yaw] at t=65.024 s: -184.418 -> -279.876 deg (step -95.458, 214.3x its usual variation)
effects.why: Large yaw excursion after the actuator saturation. Could be a consequence of loss of control.

next_action.action: Inspect ch[3] servo, linkage and output wiring; bench-test its response
next_action.why: Separates an actuator or hardware fault on ch[3] from a controller or estimator fault, which the recording cannot do (no feedback from the surface).
how: Identify from the airframe config which control surface and mixer ch[3] drives
With the aircraft safe on the bench, sweep ch[3] from 1100 to 1900 us and watch for jamming, binding or lack of motion
Check the ch[3] servo wiring, connector and power rail, and the servo-rail voltage under load
Compare the full flight log (raw IMU, battery voltage, servo-rail data) around t=52 s
next_action.conditions: Aircraft disarmed and propellers off, fully charged battery plus a repeat at a battery level close to flight end, surface unloaded then manually loaded.
next_action.baseline: Another channel (e.g. ch[1]) on the same airframe, and this flight at t<52 s where ch[3] sat near 1500 us.

outcomes.label: ch[3] jams or does not move
outcomes.means: Hardware fault on the surface, linkage or servo is the likely main cause of the late fault.
outcomes.then: Replace the part and request a repeat flight log

outcomes.label: ch[3] moves freely with full travel
outcomes.means: The stuck-at-max output is on the controller side; the controller then commands the saturation.
outcomes.then: Request raw IMU and controller logs around t=52 s

outcomes.label: Servo browns out at low rail voltage
outcomes.means: Power supply to the servo is implicated, linking to the early low-voltage warning.
outcomes.then: Request battery and rail voltage logs for the whole flight

unknowns: Which surface ch[3] drives and whether 1900 us is a commanded or a failsafe value.
Why pitch moved opposite to its setpoint at t=1-5.7 s despite a correct ch[2] output.
Whether the battery low-voltage and sensor-health events at t=1.015 s are real faults or startup artefacts.

already_answered.question: When did the control fault occur?
already_answered.answer: The first pitch divergence ran from t=0.897 s to 5.666 s. The sustained fault began at t=52.142 s, when ch[3] saturated.
already_answered.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[3]] at t=52.142 s: 1497 -> 1900 us (step 403, 201.5x its usual variation)

already_answered.question: Were there controller warnings or errors?
already_answered.answer: Yes, two at t=1.015 s: a battery low-voltage warning and a system sensor-health error. No other events in the recording.
already_answered.quote: EVENT t=1.015 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth

data_requests.what: Raw IMU, battery and servo-rail voltage, and RC/mixer logs for the whole flight
data_requests.window: Full flight, especially t=0-8 s and t=50-70 s
data_requests.why_needed: Settles whether the early divergence and the ch[3] saturation are power, sensor or controller driven, and whether they are linked.

field_questions.question: Which control surface or motor is wired to output channel ch[3]?
field_questions.why_needed: Decides which physical part to inspect and whether pitch inversion is a plausible effect of its saturation.
field_questions.not_in_data: The sheet only lists actuator.output[ch[n]]; there is no channel-to-surface mapping in the series names or events.

if_answers.means: Stuck-at-max ch[3] directly explains the pitch loss; hardware inspection takes priority.
ch[3] saturation is more likely a symptom or a contributor; pitch inversion needs another explanation (estimator or loss of control).

unobservable.fact: Whether the ch[3] servo or linkage physically jammed or failed
unobservable.why_it_matters: Distinguishes actuator hardware from controller-commanded saturation.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Bench-test the servo and linkage; inspect for binding or damage.

hypotheses.claim: The ch[3] output or surface failed or saturated at 1900 us at t=52.142 s, degrading pitch control.
hypotheses.because: ch[3] was first to leave baseline at t=52.142, stayed pinned at 1900 us, and pitch tracking degraded afterwards.
hypotheses.observed_at: controller output command (actuator.output[ch[3]]), not the physical surface

hypotheses.claim: The attitude estimate is unreliable, matching the sensor-health error and the yaw jumps, so the controller reacts to wrong data.
hypotheses.because: Sensor-health error at t=1.015 s and discontinuous yaw/pitch steps; the setpoint-opposed pitch is consistent with this, but nothing here separates it from real motion.

hypotheses.claim: A low-voltage condition caused the early throttle and pitch disturbance and could affect servo supply.
